name: Best Order to Do Roofing, Kitchen, and Bathroom Remodeling in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: How can I sequence kitchen and bathroom remodeling with roofing replacement to avoid damaging new finishes in a Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: How can I sequence kitchen and bathroom remodeling with roofing replacement to avoid damaging new finishes in a Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: On homes that need both interior remodels and a new roof, the order of work can prevent costly damage and rework. In Los Angeles, a good sequence is: 1. **Roof and structural work first**: Replace or repair roofing, sheathing, and structural members before finishing interiors. This reduces the risk of leaks damaging new cabinets, drywall, or flooring during construction or the next rainy season. 2. **Rough mechanicals**: Complete rough plumbing, electrical, HVAC ducts, and any framing modifications for new kitchen or bathroom layouts while walls and ceilings are open. If roof penetrations, new vents, or solar mounts are planned, coordinate them with the roofing contractor. 3. **Insulation and drywall**: After inspections, insulate and close walls and ceilings. 4. **Cabinets, tile, and finishes**: Only install kitchen cabinets, countertops, bathroom tile, and finish flooring once the building shell is watertight and all rough work is approved. Trying to remodel kitchens and baths before roof replacement risks moisture damage and can force contractors to open finished ceilings later for roof repairs or new penetrations. Ask your general contractor to build a written **phasing plan** that coordinates roofers, plumbers, electricians, and finish trades to prevent conflicts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan roof replacement and structural or mechanical upgrades before interior finishes. Replace the roof, complete major framing, rough plumbing, and electrical changes first, then insulate, close walls, and install kitchen and bathroom finishes so they are not exposed to leaks, debris, or structural modifications.
